Alterac Pass: Objective: free the prisoners by killing the tanky minions, then channel and hold. Cavalry pushes all three lanes and gives a push buff.
Take the siege camp as soon as it spawns and again before the objective. Respawn is roughly 90 seconds in the mid game.
One player can hold the channel because guards do not interrupt it. The others can take XP or camps and return.
Comp wants global heroes, wave clear, mercenary control and poke.

Common mistakes: collapsing the side lanes while grouped at the prison, starting the objective while behind in XP, overextending for forts, and chasing the core once it is weak because it regenerates.
Battlefield of Eternity: Objective: two Immortals, each team races the enemy one. The winner's Immortal pushes a lane.
Comp wants strong damage on the Immortal to win the race, or better teamfighting to pull the enemy off theirs.
Common mistake: committing to the race without checking that you win the damage race.
Braxis Holdout: Objective: two beacons. Both teams get Zerg waves and the winner gets the stronger one.
Comp wants sustain, duelists, displacement, reliable control and a strong solo laner.
Common mistakes: panicking when the enemy briefly holds both beacons, dying alone at a beacon, and leaving a lane open.
Cursed Hollow: Objective: three tributes. Each curses the enemy, so minions drop to one health and structures stop firing. The third tribute matters most.
Comp wants global mobility, fast rotations, wave clear and independent offlaners.
Giving up an early tribute is often better than losing several heroes to contest it. Convert a curse into lasting structure damage.
Dragon Shire: Objective: hold both shrines to activate the Dragon Knight.
Comp wants strong rotations and offlane play rather than one specific type.
Common mistake: sending all five to the middle with neither shrine controlled. If they commit to one shrine, pressure the other.
Garden of Terror: Objective: three seeds spawn a Garden Terror per lane, and Overgrowth disables enemy structures.
Push with the Terrors and use the disabled structures. When defending, destroy the Overgrowth. Three lane pressure matters.
The 28 Sep 2026 patch lowered Shambler health and damage by 25 percent at the start, growing back over the match. This is newer than most games in this tool.
Infernal Shrines: Objective: shrines summon guardians. The first team to 40 gets a Punisher. The first shrine appears about 30 seconds in and is weak.
Comp wants area damage that clears guardians. Line skillshots get eaten by guardians.
Kill the top lane Shaman first or it keeps respawning dogs. Take siege camps early. Do not fight over a weak first Punisher.
The 39 of 40 hold (leave the shrine one short and claim it when ready) is useful when the enemy is far behind.
On defense, stay back from structures because Punishers leap and stun.
Sky Temple: Objective: temples activate periodically, and holding one fires at enemy structures.
You do not need every temple. Trading one is fine, and a bad fight over a single temple is worse than giving it up.
Forts and towers lost make later temple hits more dangerous, so stack objectives.
Tomb of the Spider Queen: Objective: minions drop gems and turning in enough summons a Webweaver in each lane.
Comp wants wave clear and efficient four player rotations.
Common mistakes: hoarding gems and chasing kills while carrying a large stack.
Towers of Doom: Objective: cores start at 40 health and altars fire at the core, with damage rising as bell towers are held. Core health is a resource.
Early: sapper camps, the bottom lane is key, and the top camp supports the solo lane.
Altar channel takes about 6 seconds, so poke the channeler to interrupt. Later altars spawn about 110 seconds after the last capture.
Common mistakes: ignoring the bottom lane and treating altar shots as minor.
Volskaya Foundry: Objective: capture the large point to get the Triglav Protector. Points cycle middle, top, bottom and take about a minute to capture. One hero can hold, and contesting can push into overtime.
Fortification camps give XP and turrets. The support camp gives a Healing Pulse, so take it with a lead.
Players inside the Protector lose their own kit, so choose who goes in. Pull the tank back if the enemy engages.
Comp wants sustain and good positioning. Avoid overextending for towers.
Blackheart's Bay: Objective: collect doubloons from chests and camps and turn them in to Blackheart. The paid ship bombards enemy structures. Carried doubloons drop on death.
Protect the carrier, punish a heavily loaded enemy and turn in safely. Chasing kills while carrying a big stack is a mistake.
Hanamura Temple: Objective: stand near the contested payload to move it. Delivery fires a barrage at enemy structures. The Sentinel camp adds pushing pressure.
Comp wants heroes who hold space around the payload and give mercenary pressure. Ignoring the Sentinel is a mistake.
Haunted Mines: Objective: defeat the undead army in the mine for skulls. The team with more skulls gets the stronger Grave Golem.
The 11 May 2026 balance patch raised skull scaling and shifted Golem strength toward the late game. Frontline and sustain read as better after it, which is commentary, not data.
Do not die for small Golem upgrades, and do not abandon every lane or the enemy gets value above ground.
Warhead Junction: Objective: collect warheads and launch them at a target area. An interrupted launch penalty was reduced from 10 to 5 seconds in a July 2026 update (date unverified).
Comp wants global heroes, strong solo laners and players who track missing enemies. Aim at the most valuable structures, and do not walk alone with a warhead.
